findings.reason: the case must name the record's path as the run's declared head-keyed name, or it cannot fail on the one read path the defect actually leaves unguarded.
findings.text: the third case asserts that "a record another review run delivered for the same reviewed run and head is not filed by this run's promotion" without saying which path that record sits at; a record placed under the delivering run's own id (the shape the cited measurement left in `review-records/`) is invisible to the unchanged name-based read, so the case passes on an implementation that never filters the name arm, and the arm that must be repaired is not exercised

findings.reason: a builder implementing exactly what is written lands the content scan, leaves the name arm able to file a superseded round's record over the store's slot for that head, and the plan's own guard case does not catch it.
findings.text: the deliverable adds content-based discovery "as well as" name-based filing and claims a record another review run delivered "is never re-filed by this run's filing"; but every round of one reviewed run composes the identical declared path through `run_review_record_paths` (reckon/crew/review.py:2980), so a superseded or re-dispatched round's record IS the file the name arm opens, and `file_delivered_run_review_report` (reckon/crew/review.py:3032) filters on nothing beyond JSON readability before calling `store_review` — so the promise holds only if the name arm is also filtered on `review_run_id`, which the section never says

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `delivered_run_review_paths` (reckon/crew/review.py:2995), `file_delivered_run_reviews` (:3015), `_delivered_review_records` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:2181), `store_review` (:2856), `crew check --review` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:883) and the cited run `r-20261024T201437083115-...` all resolve, and the run's `review-records/` holds both records under `r-20261024T210701164481-review-of-...json`, as the section states.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s25's third case (`docs/plans/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion.html:2702`) does not say where the other review run's record sits, so it can pass while the name-based read still files a sibling round's record.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every log is stated to sit under the run directory, and the two `git archive` arms are on node-local scratch, which the manifest's log path makes durable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section and its write paths name the mechanism (`a_misnamed_delivered_review_is_filed`), with no plan label, ticket number or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated mechanism (content match added alongside the name match) cannot deliver the guarantee the same paragraph makes that a sibling or superseded round's record is "never re-filed by this run's filing", because a superseded round writes at the same declared name.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: filing finds a delivered record by its content, with the dry-run receipt named as the second surface of that same resolution.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s25 declares no `depends-on` and needs none: the run-review delivery contract it builds on (`run_review_record_paths`, `review-records/`) is landed, and its write paths (`reckon/crew/review.py`, `reckon/crew/promotion.py`) are already reachable without gating a landed section.
